semantics:
(identical in the Rust harness, the Python wheel driver and what the qt zoo must do):
- `events` are hbt feed rows, one hbt Event each, processed in list order, `exch_ts = local_ts = ts`.
  Timestamps are strictly increasing, so there is exactly one feed row per timestamp.
- `actions` (submit / cancel) happen at `ts` with zero order latency: the action is issued after every feed row
  with `ts_row <= ts` has been processed and the exchange processes it before any feed row with `ts_row > ts`
  (hbt EventSet tie-break: ExchData before ExchOrder at equal timestamps; actions here never share a feed ts).
- trade rows carry `aggressor` ("B" buyer-initiated -> hbt BUY_EVENT, hits resting asks; "A" seller-initiated ->
  hbt SELL_EVENT, hits resting bids).  depth/snapshot rows carry the book `side` and the NEW absolute level qty.

Cancel to 12, delete level (qty 0), re-add 15, trade 1
Three own orders at one level: each sees the full trade (no shared budget) and Q at arrival excludes earlier own orders
Bid at 100 and ask at 101 live together; trades and cancels on both sides
Sell trade below a bid and buy trade above an ask fill fully (maker)
Opposite best moves onto the order price (depth row): full fill via best update
DEPTH_CLEAR does not touch own-order queue state; the snapshot row arrives with prev_qty=0
Own order cancelled; later trades must not fill it
Depth qty 0.3 < half lot deletes the level in the book but the queue model sees new_qty=0.3; the next row at that price then has prev_qty=0
GTX bid at the best ask and GTX ask at the best bid expire on arrival
lot 0.5: -F/L half-lot rounding, partial 0.5 then filled==leaves (#312) then error
Feed sends the depth decrease before the trade: the trade is counted twice (cancel inference + trade)
Several trades accumulate T before one depth row; partial netting leaves a net cancel
Ask order at 102 (second level) with cancels ahead/behind; buy trades at 101 do not touch it
